prompt: Stage 5-2, level 9, 48 HP, 3 players left with you. Your board holds two 2-star 1-costs for a trait breakpoint. You have 60 gold and the shop shows a 5-cost that fits your board. What is the play?

options.label: Keep the 1-costs: the trait breakpoint is worth more than a 1-star 5-cost
Buy the 5-cost tank, sell a 1-cost, and roll for a second 5-cost with the rest
Save toward level 10 to fit everything

explanation:
At level 9 in a 4-player lobby, board cap decides placements. A 2-star 1-cost on a level-9 board is a unit that dies in two seconds regardless of the breakpoint it enables; the breakpoint bonus is designed for stage 3 boards. A 1-star 5-cost tank has more raw stats than both 1-costs together and a game-changing ability. With 60 gold you buy it, sell the weaker 1-cost, and roll for a second 5-cost or the 2-star on your caster: those are the upgrades that win fights against capped boards.

Level 10 is 60 XP away and would cost every gold you have for one more slot, arriving at 6-1 if you survive. Three players are already capped; you cannot afford to be the one still building.
principle: At level 9 your board is judged by its weakest unit. Trait breakpoints do not excuse a 1-cost.
commonMistake: Valuing a trait tier over unit quality because the trait icon turns gold.
